purpose: Authoritative-vendor manufacturing integration delta. Adds Seeq and Canary Historian as distinct industrial analytics/historian targets, reusing existing REST/OData and REST/Protobuf RPC over HTTP/2 profiles. Evidence remains specification/public-documentation level only: no sandbox or customer tenant credentials were used and all writes remain disabled.

systems.name: Seeq
systems.evidenceNote: Seeq documents its Server REST API as the interface used by the Seeq web application for the capabilities exposed in Workbench and Organizer, with SDKs derived from that REST API. Seeq also exposes modern OData 4.0 exports for Items, Samples, Capsules and statistics/metadata. Legacy OData is deprecated and, according to current Seeq deprecation guidance, fully removed in July 2026, so Manufacturing WFM must use the modern /odata/{id}.svc route only. Authentication varies by deployment and can include OAuth/OpenID Connect/session authentication or Seeq Access Keys; access keys inherit their owner's permissions and therefore are not intrinsically least privilege. No Seeq sandbox or tenant authentication was attempted.

requiredPermissions: customer-authorised Seeq identity limited to the analyses, assets, signals and exports required by WFM
read-only REST access to required signals, conditions, asset metadata and analytical results
modern OData 4.0 export read access only where a customer uses an export as the governed hand-off
no workbook, calculation, asset, user, connector, export-definition or other mutative permission during discovery
access keys, when unavoidable, must belong to a narrowly scoped non-admin service identity and be vaulted/rotated at the executor boundary
dataAvailableOrExpected: time-series signals and sampled values exposed to authorised Seeq users
asset paths, item metadata, units and descriptions
calculated or derived signals and analytics created in Seeq
modern OData Items, Samples, Capsules and statistical result tables where the customer has configured exports
workbook/worksheet context and analytical results reachable through the authorised REST surface
automationOpportunities: consume customer-governed downtime, operating-state or anomaly calculations as labour-demand and redeployment signals
correlate shift staffing and labour cost with contextualised production, equipment and energy analytics
use conditions/capsules to distinguish sustained disruption from transient telemetry noise before recommending labour moves
reuse Seeq analytics already approved by operations/engineering instead of recreating calculations inside WFM
detect stale exports, changed item IDs, changed asset paths and calculation/schema drift before derived signals affect workforce decisions
consider any Seeq-side creation/update or outward webhook/callback only after a separately authorised write-roundtrip proof
savingsHypotheses: reduce duplicate OT analytics engineering by consuming customer-approved Seeq signals and conditions
reduce paid idle labour by responding to trustworthy sustained downtime/recovery conditions
reduce overstaffing or understaffing by combining Seeq production analytics with WFM demand and availability
reduce manual shift-performance analysis by joining labour outcomes to contextualised industrial analytics
reduce implementation effort where Seeq already normalises multiple historian/OT sources
dataGaps: Seeq is not normally the authoritative source for worker identity, employment, payroll, absence or roster truth
signals, calculations, conditions, asset paths and workbook semantics are customer-specific and require explicit canonical mapping
a calculated or interpolated Seeq value is not automatically equivalent to a raw machine observation
available APIs, analytical objects and authentication patterns vary by Seeq release and cloud/on-prem deployment
modern OData exports expose customer-selected analytical outputs rather than a universal manufacturing object model
constraintsRisks: derived/calculated values can be filtered, interpolated, aggregated, delayed or otherwise transformed; WFM must preserve raw-versus-derived lineage, source/event time, calculation identity and quality semantics
Access Keys inherit the owner's permissions, so using an over-privileged owner would defeat read-only intent
session-cookie REST authentication can require x-sq-csrf handling; OAuth/CORS flows can retrieve the CSRF token through the documented auth endpoint
legacy OData must not be selected for new connectors because the vendor removal timeline has passed
large time-range reads and analytical exports require bounded windows, backpressure and pagination/streaming behaviour appropriate to the selected Seeq endpoint
on-prem Seeq servers and remote data sources can sit behind plant/network boundaries; WFM must use customer-approved routing and must not scan source historians or PLC networks directly
Seeq REST capabilities can include mutations; read-only safety must be enforced by identity/operation allowlists, not by HTTP method convention alone
valueReview.nextDevelopmentAction: Reuse the existing REST and OData profiles for a thin Seeq adapter. Require modern OData 4.0 when OData is selected, add REST capability/version discovery, CSRF/session handling where applicable, least-privilege access-key/OIDC checks, bounded time windows, canonical signal/condition/asset mapping, raw-versus-derived lineage and transformation metadata, quality/timestamp preservation and schema/item fingerprints. Then obtain an authorised Seeq test environment for least-privilege authentication and a representative read round-trip before considering any mutative Seeq operation.

systems.name: Canary Historian
systems.evidenceNote: Canary documents a Web Read API over HTTPS and a native gRPC Read API over HTTPS, both routed through the Views service. Version 26 documentation maps API tokens to Canary users and permits Tag Security to restrict the user to read access on approved Views. The separate Store and Forward write API requires write permission and is deliberately excluded from the Manufacturing WFM connector. Current documentation also distinguishes secure read endpoints from older compatibility behaviour and documents Views as the governed query/security layer over Historian data. No Canary installation, sandbox or customer historian was authenticated or queried.

requiredPermissions: dedicated Canary service user mapped to an API token and limited to Read permission on only the approved View/tag hierarchy
Views Read API access only; no Store and Forward Write API permission
TLS-secured Web Read API or native gRPC Read API endpoint exposed through the customer-approved edge/network boundary
Tag Security enabled where customer policy requires tag/asset-level restriction
no Historian administration, collector configuration, Store and Forward mutation or write permission
dataAvailableOrExpected: historian tags and tag hierarchy visible through approved Views
tag metadata and customer-defined asset/virtual-view context
events and calculations exposed through the customer's Views configuration where available
quality/status context carried by the customer's historian data and selected query path
contextualised views over data collected from upstream OPC UA, MQTT/Sparkplug, SQL, CSV and other configured sources
automationOpportunities: use trusted machine-state and downtime history to refresh labour-demand and redeployment recommendations
correlate staffed time with output, runtime, stoppage and recovery history by work centre
reuse Canary Views as a governed aggregation boundary for legacy and mixed-protocol plant sources rather than connecting WFM directly to each source
use historical patterns to forecast labour needs around recurring production, downtime or maintenance conditions
detect stale Views/tag mappings, historian gaps and quality degradation before operational signals influence live workforce decisions
consider historian writes only if a future business case exists and after separate Store and Forward sandbox write/read-back certification
savingsHypotheses: reduce bespoke connector engineering by using the customer's existing historian and Views layer
reduce paid idle labour by detecting and analysing machine stoppage/recovery earlier
reduce emergency overtime by correlating recurring historian patterns with maintenance and skills demand
reduce manual production/labour reconciliation through shift-aligned historical queries
extend WFM analytics to older plants without replacing their existing collection stack
dataGaps: tag names, hierarchy, virtual Views and asset semantics are customer-specific
historian data does not normally establish worker identity, payroll, qualification or authoritative schedule truth
upstream collectors can differ by site and may provide different timestamp, quality or engineering-unit semantics
the exact gRPC schema/documentation is installation/version specific and must be matched to the customer's deployed Canary release
historical interpolation, aggregation or calculated tags must be distinguished from raw observations
constraintsRisks: API tokens are mapped to Canary users; the token is only as least-privileged as that user's Views/Tag Security permissions
Read and Write APIs coexist in the product but are separate authorities; WFM must technically exclude Store and Forward write access
large historian ranges require bounded time windows, sampling/downsampling awareness, backpressure and durable checkpoints
quality, source timestamps and transformation/aggregation metadata must be preserved so historical/processed data cannot masquerade as current raw state
Canary documentation notes historian files are not encrypted at rest by the product itself, so customers requiring at-rest encryption need encrypted storage/volume controls outside the connector
on-prem historian endpoints must remain behind a customer-controlled edge/network boundary; WFM cloud must not directly scan plant networks
virtual Views can rebuild as underlying tags change, so tag/view schema fingerprints and customer mappings need drift detection
valueReview.nextDevelopmentAction: Reuse the existing REST and Protobuf RPC/HTTP2 profiles for a thin Canary Views Read adapter. Extend the reusable fabric to allow a system to require a customer edge even when its exposed protocol is HTTPS/gRPC, then add Canary version detection, explicit secure Views endpoint binding, read-token permission checks, bounded history windows, tag/view schema fingerprints, source-time/quality/transformation preservation and customer asset/work-centre mappings. Validate web and gRPC fixtures without any write route, then obtain an authorised lab/customer historian for least-privilege authentication and a representative read round-trip.
